faq_bestUpgrade: What should I buy first in Crunch My Butter?
faq_bestUpgrade_answer: Better butter almost always wins. EX10 describes the loop as "unlock better butter", which makes flavor tier the primary multiplier on cash per crunch — that is why butter unlocks sit at S on our tier list. Roller upgrades come second at A, because they raise throughput so the richer butter actually gets crunched. Area expansion is a strong B once your roller has spare capacity, and pure manual crunching without reinvesting is a C-tier dead end after the first few minutes.
faq_butterFlavors: How many butter flavors are there?
faq_butterFlavors_answer: Nobody has published a complete flavor list yet, and we refuse to invent one. The only flavor confirmed by official art is Salted Butter, which appears on the game icon and thumbnail as the entry tier of the ladder. Every additional flavor is bought with collected cash, and the in-game prompt shows the exact price and payout before you confirm. We are cataloguing the rest from live sessions and will publish names only after confirming them in-game.

faq_hasCodes_answer: No. As of July 26, 2026 Crunch My Butter has no redeem box anywhere in the game and no working code has ever been verified. faq_howToPlay: How do you play Crunch My Butter?
faq_howToPlay_answer: Join a server and roll over the starter Salted Butter until its crunchy shell cracks. Every crack drops cash onto your floor, and nothing is banked until you pick it up. Spend that cash on the next butter flavor to raise your income per crunch, upgrade your roller so each pass crunches more butter per motion, then expand your butter area once your roller can cover it. Repeat the loop — the idle layer keeps earning while you are offline.
faq_isFree: Is Crunch My Butter free to play?
faq_isFree_answer: Yes. Crunch My Butter is a free Roblox experience that you launch from the Roblox app on phone, tablet, PC or console. At the time of writing it ships with no Game Passes at all, so there is nothing to buy inside the game and no paid shortcut past the butter ladder. Progression comes entirely from crunching, collecting and reinvesting cash, plus the offline earnings layer that runs while you are away.
faq_offlineCash: Does Crunch My Butter earn cash offline?
faq_offlineCash_answer: Yes. EX10’s own tagline for the game is "EARN CASH WHILE YOU SLEEP", so offline accumulation is a designed part of the economy rather than a bug or an exploit. The exact rate and any cap are not published, so treat any site quoting a specific cash-per-hour figure with suspicion. In practice the routine that works is simple: collect your offline cash first at session start, immediately buy the next unlock, then start crunching.
faq_rollerVsButter: Should I upgrade my roller or unlock better butter?
faq_rollerVsButter_answer: Compare the two prices against the income each one adds and buy whichever costs less per unit of income gained. As a rule of thumb, upgrade the roller first when your butter is already crunching faster than you can roll over it, and unlock better butter first when your roller already sweeps the whole floor between respawns. After every roller purchase, re-check whether your butter area has become too small for the new sweep speed.

A larger floor also increases the cash your butter generates while you are offline, so it compounds overnight. Pair each expansion with the next butter flavor and re-measure cash per minute afterwards.

category_intro_guides: Crunch My Butter is built around a single deceptively simple loop — crunch flavored butter, collect the cash it drops, unlock better butter, upgrade your roller, and expand your butter floor. That five-step cycle is the entire game. Every mechanic, every upgrade, and every cash strategy in this wiki is a variation on that one loop. The beginner section teaches you to run the loop in the right order so you never stall on your starter Salted Butter. The order matters because each track — butter flavor, roller throughput, butter area, and offline accumulation — feeds the others. Buying expensive butter before your roller is fast enough just starves your cash flow. Expanding your floor before you have rollers to cover it wastes both money and idle income. Guides are written for first-time Roblox players, returning players coming back after the Update 2 event, and experienced incremental simulator fans who want the decision framework rather than the raw numbers. We avoid invented item names, fabricated tutorial steps, or claims about systems the game does not visibly contain — everything below is anchored in the official game description, the verified Update 2 event listing, and direct observation of the live experience.

category_mechanics_guides: The four-track progression is what makes Crunch My Butter feel like a real incremental simulator rather than a casual mini-game. Each track has its own scaling curve and its own ceiling, and the tracks interact multiplicatively rather than additively — buying a more expensive butter flavor before upgrading your roller means the new flavor's higher cash per crunch is bottlenecked by the slow roller, so your effective income barely moves. The official description names the loop in five words — crunch, collect, unlock, upgrade, expand — and each of those five words corresponds to one of the four tracks plus the collection step. The collection step itself is where many new players lose time, because dropped cash sits on the floor until collected and the idle timer does not credit you for cash you have not picked up. The offline earnings system sits on top of all four tracks and is the reason EX10 markets the game with "earn cash while you sleep" — the multipliers from your butter, roller, and floor combine and accumulate while you are away. The mechanics favor patience and reinvestment over hoarding. A player who sits on a large cash balance is leaving compounding income on the table because every idle minute spent sitting on unspent cash is income they are not earning. Understanding these interactions is the only skill the game actually tests.
category_advantages_guides: Crunch My Butter is one of the most accessible incremental simulators on Roblox. The 8-player server size removes queue anxiety and lets new players join without waiting, the lack of voice chat and camera keeps the experience low-pressure, and the 93 percent approval rating across more than 15,000 votes suggests the existing player base finds the loop rewarding rather than punishing. Crucially, there are no Game Passes, no badges, and no developer products in the current build, which means every player has the same access to every track — there is no pay-to-skip mechanic sitting between you and the late butter tiers. The ASMR focus (crunch sounds, squishy physics, soft body deformation) means the game is also pleasant to watch even when you are not actively optimizing. For a parent or older sibling worried about Roblox safety, the rating and the lack of microtransactions make this a relatively low-risk first experience. For a returning player coming back to check on Update 2, the four-track progression gives you a clear checklist of what to verify has changed and what should still feel the same. The advantages are not about being the best — this is not a PvP game — but about having a satisfying long-tail progression that rewards short sessions and long sessions equally.
category_weaknesses_guides: The biggest weakness of the current build is information scarcity. As of the last verification, EX10 has not published a butter flavor price list, a roller upgrade cost table, or area expansion multipliers anywhere in the game or on official channels. The Roblox API confirms zero Game Passes, zero badges, and zero developer products, which means the wiki cannot link to a definitive source for any of those numbers. This forces us to describe progression in qualitative terms — "buy the next flavor when it is cheaper than your current roller upgrade" rather than "buy at 50,000 cash" — and means our advice can be invalidated by a single balance change. Players who prefer spreadsheet-driven optimization will find this frustrating. The 8-player server cap can also create wait times during peak hours, especially after a content update when every existing player logs in at once. The ASMR aesthetic, while pleasant, is subjective — players who do not enjoy crunch and squishy sounds will not find the core loop compelling even if the numbers are optimal. There is no rebirthing or prestige system confirmed as of this writing, which means long-term progression is purely additive and the late game is unlikely to feel like a fresh start. Finally, the game is still less than five weeks old at the time of writing, which means everything described above is subject to change when Update 2 lands on August 1, 2026 at 17:00 UTC.

category_faq_guides_a_1: Crunch My Butter is designed for both short and long sessions. Longer sessions (30 minutes or more) let you ride the offline income curve up by reinvesting repeatedly. Most players report 20 to 40 minute sessions as the sweet spot before the diminishing returns of the current butter tier kick in. Because the offline layer keeps accumulating, leaving after a strong session and returning later is often more efficient than grinding the same tier past its breakpoint.

You and your friends can join the same server and crunch side by side, but each player runs their own instance of the four-track progression. The 8-player cap is on the low end for Roblox and means you may have to refresh the server browser to find a slot during peak hours, especially after Update 2 when existing players log in to check the new content. Second, real code lists include expiry dates. Fake lists either omit dates or list impossibly long expiry windows ("active until December 2099"). Third, real code strings match the format the developer has used in their other games — if EX10 uses alphanumeric codes of eight characters in their other titles, a "code" of thirty characters is suspicious. Fourth, real lists update frequently; fake lists are stuck on the same content from launch week. Fifth, real lists have at least one code that has actually expired and is marked as such. Fake lists claim every code is still active forever.

category_mechanics_butter-flavors: Butter flavor progression is the first of the four progression tracks and the one most players will encounter within their first ten minutes. Each flavor multiplies the cash dropped per crunch, which means the gap between consecutive flavors widens as you climb — a 2x multiplier feels manageable from the starter tier but compounds into a noticeable jump by the mid-game. The interesting design choice in Crunch My Butter is that the multipliers interact with the roller, not just with each other. A more expensive butter with a slow roller still bottlenecks on the roller, which is why the official description puts unlock before upgrade — the loop assumes you will buy the next flavor first and then realize your roller is the constraint. The visual and audio signature of each flavor is also part of the progression, though we cannot describe flavors we have not confirmed. The Salted Butter wrap is dark blue with bold yellow text, the cream rendering is warm beige with high gloss, and the crunch sound is a sharp crack followed by a soft squelch. Higher tiers presumably escalate on all three axes — visual richness, gloss intensity, and crunch sharpness — but that is inference, not observation. The offline income layer reads the current butter flavor at the moment you leave the game and applies its multiplier to whatever cash your roller produces while you are away. This means the flavor you choose at the moment you go AFK is the flavor that drives your idle income, which is one reason experienced players avoid buying a flavor they cannot afford to stay on for at least a few minutes.
category_advantages_butter-flavors: Salted Butter is the best starter flavor in the game by default — it is the only one we can confirm exists, which means every player starts on it and the economy is calibrated around it. The visual design is striking (deep blue wrap, gold yellow text, warm cream butter) and the audio signature is satisfying for ASMR fans. For new players, the practical advantage of starting on Salted Butter is that the early-game math is straightforward: every crunch produces the same amount of cash, so you can build an intuition for cash per minute without juggling flavor multipliers. For returning players, the advantage of confirming only Salted Butter is that you are not chasing flavor names that may not exist — you can focus your optimization on the roller and the floor instead, which are the two tracks with more visible returns. The honest acknowledgment of what we do not know (the full flavor list, the price table, the multiplier curve) is itself an advantage, because it protects you from buying into a wiki that pretends to know more than it does. Our wiki only lists flavors that are visible in the official assets. Anything else would be fabrication.

Every incremental simulator wiki eventually becomes a tier list, and Crunch My Butter's wiki cannot do that yet without inventing flavor names. The result is that this page is shorter and less visually rich than the corresponding pages on more mature game wikis. Players who want a flavor tier ranking will need to wait until either the game publishes a price list, the EX10 developer group posts a roadmap, or Update 2 on August 1, 2026 introduces a confirmed new flavor. Another weakness is that the visual upgrade curve between flavors is invisible to us — we can describe Salted Butter's appearance with confidence but cannot tell you what the next tier looks like without speculating. If EX10 ever updates the icon to feature a different flavor, the "current confirmed flavor" answer here will need to be re-verified. We do not have a way to monitor that automatically, so the page relies on the same daily verification cadence as the rest of the wiki. category_intro_roller-upgrades: Roller upgrades are the throughput track in Crunch My Butter. A faster roller does not change the cash value of a single crunch; it changes how many butter passes you complete during an active session and how much of your floor the idle system can cover while you are away. EX10 calls the tool a roller in the official description, and that is the only confirmed terminology — there is no public list of named roller tiers, costs, or speed percentages. This page therefore focuses on the decision process rather than invented numbers. Measure your cash per minute on the current roller, read the exact next-upgrade price shown in the live game, and compare the payback time to the next butter flavor. Also compare coverage: a wider butter floor with a slow roller creates uncovered space that produces less than it should. Roller upgrades are most valuable when your butter flavor has already improved but your cash curve has flattened because you cannot crunch quickly enough. They are less valuable when the roller has spare capacity and your active butter area is tiny. The right purchase changes as your area expands, so re-test after every expansion instead of assuming the old order remains optimal.

category_mechanics_roller-upgrades: Roller throughput is the second progression line and the easiest one to misunderstand. The tool determines how much butter you process per movement, how quickly the shell cracks, and whether your active route can keep the floor clear. In practical terms, your income per minute is a product of butter value and roller throughput, multiplied by how consistently you keep moving. An upgrade that doubles speed is wasted if you only use it on a tiny starter patch; an upgrade that improves coverage is valuable after an expansion because it converts newly available surface into actual crunches. The in-game price prompt is the authoritative source for cost and effect. We do not publish guessed tier names or percentage gains because no verified table exists. Instead, use a simple payback test: record cash before a one-minute active run, buy the upgrade, repeat the same route for one minute, and compare the difference. The upgrade is economically sound when the added cash per minute repays its price before your next planned idle window. Remember that offline income uses the same roller capacity, so a roller that is too slow during an overnight session can underperform even when it feels adequate during a short active run.
category_advantages_roller-upgrades: Roller upgrades reward players who observe their own bottleneck instead of buying on a fixed checklist. They improve both active play and offline accumulation, making them one of the few purchases that matter across the entire progression curve. A well-timed upgrade also makes the ASMR experience smoother: fewer pauses, fewer awkward repositioning movements, and a more continuous crack-and-squelch rhythm. Because the game has no PvP, there is no pressure to match another player's speed or chase a leaderboard; you can make the purchase that fits your own session length. The upgrade decision is also easy to explain to a new player: if butter is waiting to be crunched, improve the roller; if the roller is idle, improve the butter. This clear signal makes the category approachable even without a public numerical database. Finally, the lack of Game Passes means every player can reach the same roller performance through ordinary reinvestment, so the advice applies equally to free players and players who simply prefer not to spend Robux.
category_weaknesses_roller-upgrades: The weakness is that precise roller tables are not available. We cannot responsibly list the names of every tier, exact costs, speed multipliers, or a best-in-slot ranking because EX10 has not published those figures and community pages have not verified them. A second weakness is that roller performance is route-dependent: two players can buy the same upgrade and see different cash-per-minute gains because one sweeps a larger area, leaves cash uncollected, or plays on a phone with different movement friction. The payback test therefore requires a little discipline and cannot be reduced to one universal answer. A third weakness is that the game may rebalance throughput when Update 2 lands. If EX10 changes how quickly the roller moves or how much butter a pass covers, old observations become historical rather than current guidance. Treat any screenshot or video that claims a permanent percentage as a timestamped snapshot, not a promise. We will update this page when direct values are confirmed, but until then the decision framework is more reliable than a fabricated spreadsheet.

It does not replace the butter flavor multiplier; it works alongside it. A high-value butter with a slow roller can still earn less than a cheaper butter that your roller clears continuously. Read the in-game prompt for the exact effect and judge the purchase by your own cash per minute.
category_faq_roller-upgrades_q_1: When should I buy a roller upgrade?
category_faq_roller-upgrades_a_1: Buy when the roller is the bottleneck. You will see butter waiting uncrunched, long pauses between cracks, or cash growth flattening even though you recently improved the butter flavor. Compare the roller price with the next flavor price and estimate payback from a one-minute test. If the roller already clears your current floor with spare capacity, the next flavor usually gives a better return.

A roller that cannot cover the butter area efficiently leaves offline potential unused. Before logging off, make sure your current floor is reachable by the roller and that you have reinvested any available cash rather than leaving a large unspent balance.

Expansion increases the amount of butter available, but a roller upgrade determines whether you can process that extra area. If your current roller already sweeps the whole floor with time to spare, expansion can come first; otherwise upgrade throughput and then expand. This is a coverage decision, not a fixed rule.

category_intro_cash-farming: Cash farming in Crunch My Butter is not a separate minigame; it is the discipline of running the crunch loop so every minute produces the most banked cash possible. The official cycle tells you exactly what to do: crunch flavored butter, collect cash from the butter, unlock better butter, upgrade your roller, and expand your butter. The hard part is order and consistency. Cash drops on the floor and remains uncollected, so a player who crunches quickly but never sweeps their area can look productive while losing bankable income. The idle layer adds another dimension: EX10 explicitly markets the game with "earn cash while you sleep", so your final layout and active upgrades continue to matter after you leave. This page covers active crunch rhythm, collection sweeps, session-start order, reinvestment, CPM measurement, and AFK setup without inventing rates or caps. No reliable public source lists the exact offline rate, so measure your own account. The framework is designed for a new player on Salted Butter, a returning player checking a changed balance after Update 2, or an experienced incremental player who wants to compare active and idle returns. The rule is simple: bank cash, reinvest quickly, and never let an avoidable bottleneck sit idle.

category_mechanics_cash-farming: Cash farming has four moving parts. Active crunching creates drops; collection turns drops into a banked balance; reinvestment converts that balance into a higher future rate; and offline accumulation extends the same rate while you are away. The order is important because cash that is still sitting on the floor cannot fund the next purchase, while cash left unspent cannot compound. Start each session by collecting offline cash, then buy the next affordable upgrade, then begin an uninterrupted crunch route. During active play, alternate between a consistent roller sweep and a short floor collection loop. Measure CPM with a fixed one-minute or five-minute sample rather than intuition, because one lucky collection burst can make a route look better than it is. Offline earnings are a multiplier on the layout you leave behind, not a magic replacement for progression: a small floor with a slow roller produces less while you sleep than a fully covered floor with reinvested cash. The game currently exposes no confirmed numerical cap, so record your own before-and-after totals and label them with a date. This also gives you a clean baseline after Update 2 changes any economy values.
category_advantages_cash-farming: The advantage of a cash-farming framework is that it works with confirmed facts rather than guessed rates. You do not need to know an exact hourly payout to know that collecting cash is better than leaving it on the floor, or that buying a productive upgrade is better than hoarding the same balance. The method also scales to any play style. A child playing for ten minutes can perform a collection sweep and one reinvestment; a serious player can run a CPM experiment across several routes; an AFK player can set up a productive layout before closing the app. Because the game is free to play with no Game Passes, the resulting cash curve is not distorted by paid multipliers. The ASMR design makes repeated routes tolerable, and the small server cap means you can focus on your own floor without PvP pressure. Most importantly, cash farming creates a feedback loop: every measurement tells you whether the next purchase improved the economy, and every reinvestment makes the next measurement easier. That turns a vague simulator into a sequence of observable decisions.
category_weaknesses_cash-farming: Cash farming is vulnerable to small interruptions. If you stop the roller between passes, leave dropped cash uncollected, or spend ten minutes walking to an uncovered corner, your observed CPM falls even though the underlying upgrades did not change. The lack of official numerical data is another limitation: we cannot promise an hourly rate, offline cap, or exact break-even time, and a player should never copy a number without checking the date and the live prompt. Mobile input can make a route feel slower than PC input, so one universal "best route" does not exist. The offline layer may also have limits or maintenance behavior that EX10 has not documented publicly; treat the tagline as proof of the mechanic, not proof of an unlimited rate. Finally, cash farming can become repetitive if you optimize only for the number. The game is intentionally relaxing and ASMR-focused, so a route that earns five percent less but feels pleasant may be the better long-session choice. Efficient does not have to mean stressful.
category_faq_cash-farming_q_0: How do I earn cash fastest?
category_faq_cash-farming_a_0: Keep a continuous crunch rhythm, collect drops frequently, and reinvest immediately. Start by collecting offline cash, buy the next productive upgrade, then run a fixed route for one minute to measure your CPM. Compare the result after each purchase. There is no verified universal hourly number because EX10 has not published the economy table, so your own dated measurement is more trustworthy than a third-party screenshot.
category_faq_cash-farming_a_1: Cash drops on the floor around your butter area and stays there until you collect it. The cash has been earned mechanically, but it is not useful for purchases until it is banked. Make floor sweeps part of your routine instead of waiting until the whole area is covered. A clean collection route often improves practical income more than a small theoretical upgrade.
category_faq_cash-farming_q_2: Is active play better than offline income?
category_faq_cash-farming_a_2: Active play normally gives you more control because you can keep the roller moving, collect cash, and buy upgrades immediately. Offline income is valuable for long breaks and overnight windows, but its return depends on the butter flavor, roller coverage, and floor state you leave behind. Use active sessions to build the layout, then use offline time to let that layout compound.
category_faq_cash-farming_q_3: Should I save cash for a big upgrade?
category_faq_cash-farming_a_3: Only when the next purchase is genuinely close and the waiting period is short. In most cases, reinvesting sooner is better because the new multiplier earns cash during the time you would otherwise spend saving. The exception is a purchase that would not improve your bottleneck, such as expansion when the roller cannot cover the new space. Compare expected payback rather than following a hoarding habit.
category_qt_cash-farming_0: Collect before you buy. A floor sweep converts already-earned drops into the balance needed for your next upgrade and costs no Robux, no code, and no extra system.
category_qt_cash-farming_1: Use the same route for CPM tests. Changing your movement path, butter flavor, or collection timing between samples makes the comparison noisy and can trick you into buying a weaker upgrade.
category_qt_cash-farming_2: Reinvest at the start and end of a session. Start by spending collected offline cash on the best bottleneck fix; finish by leaving no large idle balance and a fully covered floor for the next offline window.
category_qt_cash-farming_3: Treat offline earnings as a multiplier, not a substitute. If your active layout is inefficient, leaving it running overnight only compounds an inefficient state.

category_intro_expansion: Expansion grows the butter area where Crunch My Butter happens. It is the fourth track in the official loop and the one most likely to be purchased too early. More surface can increase active and offline income, but only if your roller can reach the added area and your butter flavor produces enough value to justify the extra floor. The game does not publicly document the number of expansion stages, the price of each stage, or a confirmed multiplier, and no source has verified a rebirth or prestige system. We therefore treat expansion as a coverage and payback decision rather than a list of named zones. Before buying, check three prerequisites: your current roller should clear the existing floor without long pauses, you should have a butter flavor whose multiplier is still producing useful cash, and the expansion price should have a realistic payback inside your normal play or idle window. Expansion is strongest when roller throughput and offline time are both underused. It is weakest when you are still struggling to process the starter floor. This page explains the non-linear relationship between area and income, how to diagnose a late-game plateau, and why every expansion should be followed by a coverage test. The goal is productive surface, not surface for its own sake.

category_mechanics_expansion: Expansion changes the geometry of the economy. If your roller clears one compact floor continuously, adding a second area can increase the number of butter passes available, but only the covered portion contributes to actual throughput. The useful quantity is not total square footage; it is productive coverage per minute. That is why expansion has a non-linear feel: the first extra space may be easy to cover and improve income, while a later expansion can create a large uncovered zone that adds cost without adding cash. Offline earnings amplify the same effect because the game calculates from the state you leave behind. A larger floor with insufficient roller reach may look impressive but earn less overnight than a smaller floor that is fully serviced. Expansion also interacts with butter flavor: a low-value starter butter on a giant floor can produce a lot of movement without enough cash per crunch to justify the purchase. Use a three-step test after every expansion. First, walk the full area and note uncovered sections. Second, run a fixed CPM sample on the old route and the new route. Third, leave the game for a short, known interval and compare idle cash. If all three improve, the expansion is productive. If only the visual size improves, save for throughput instead.
category_advantages_expansion: Expansion offers the clearest feeling of progress in Crunch My Butter. The floor grows, the roller route becomes more expressive, and the ASMR loop gains a satisfying sense of space. It is also the progression track that helps offline players most when the prerequisites are met: more productive surface means more potential cash while you sleep. Expansion is flexible enough to fit different play styles. A mobile player can keep a compact, easy-to-sweep floor, while a PC player can exploit a larger route with precise movement. Because the game is free to play and has no confirmed PvP, there is no social pressure to expand at a particular pace. You can wait until the purchase pays for itself without falling behind a competitor. The decision framework also protects your cash: instead of treating every expansion as automatically good, you ask whether the roller, butter, and idle window are aligned. That makes expansion a meaningful strategic choice rather than a button you press whenever you have enough money.
category_weaknesses_expansion: The biggest weakness is the missing stage data. There is no verified list of expansion names, costs, dimensions, or income multipliers, so a player cannot follow a universal zone-by-zone route. The second weakness is that area is harder to measure than a simple speed stat. Coverage depends on movement, device, floor layout, and collection habits, which means two players may report different payback periods for the same purchase. The third weakness is the unresolved end-game question. Rebirth or prestige has not been confirmed, and the current public description does not mention a reset layer, so we cannot promise that a large floor eventually converts into a new cycle. Expansion may be a terminal progression line in the current build, or it may become the foundation for a future update. Update 2 is scheduled for August 1, 2026 but has no patch notes, so any guide claiming a specific new zone before launch is speculation. Keep dated notes, verify the live layout, and be willing to revise your route after every patch.
category_faq_expansion_a_0: Expand when your current roller clears the existing floor with spare capacity and the added space has a reasonable payback window. If butter is already waiting uncrunched, expansion will magnify the bottleneck rather than fix it. Check the price prompt, test coverage, and compare the expected active or offline return before confirming.
category_faq_expansion_a_1: It can, because a larger productive floor gives the roller more butter to process while you are away. The important word is productive: uncovered space contributes little or nothing if the roller cannot reach it. Leave the game with a route that covers the full floor and with cash reinvested, then measure a known idle interval to see the actual effect on your account.
category_faq_expansion_a_2: No rebirth or prestige system has been confirmed. The official game description lists crunching, collecting, unlocking, upgrading, and expanding but does not mention resets. We keep the keyword visible because players search for it, yet any article or video that promises a rebirth requirement should be treated as unverified until EX10 adds the mechanic.
category_faq_expansion_q_3: Why did my expansion not improve income?
category_faq_expansion_a_3: Usually because the roller cannot cover the new area, the new route leaves cash uncollected, or your butter flavor is too low-value to justify the added surface. Repeat the coverage test, run a fixed CPM sample, and compare against the pre-expansion route. If the new area is mostly idle, upgrade throughput before expanding again.
category_qt_expansion_0: Walk the full floor immediately after expanding. Mark any corner that the roller cannot reach without a long reposition; that is your next throughput problem.
category_qt_expansion_1: Do not expand just because the button is affordable. Compare the expansion cost with the extra cash you expect during your normal session or idle window, and postpone it if the payback is unclear.
category_qt_expansion_2: Keep mobile layouts compact. Touch movement makes huge floors harder to sweep, so a smaller fully covered area can outperform a larger area with missed corners.
category_qt_expansion_3: Record expansion observations with dates. Update 2 may change floor size, pricing, or offline behavior, and dated notes stop you from treating an old balance snapshot as current.

category_intro_tier-list: This Crunch My Butter tier list ranks progression decisions, not invented butter names or roller tiers. The public game data confirms the four-track loop but does not publish enough numerical detail to rank every individual item. Instead, we rank the tracks by the conditions under which they create value: butter unlocks multiply the cash value of each crunch, roller upgrades increase throughput, expansion adds productive surface, and manual crunching creates the baseline activity that powers all three. The tier labels are a decision aid, not a promise that one purchase is always correct. A butter unlock can be S-tier early and merely A-tier when the roller is the bottleneck. A roller upgrade can be the best purchase after expansion but unnecessary on a tiny starter floor. Area expansion is valuable when coverage is ready and weak when it creates unused space. Manual crunching is essential at the start but becomes a C-tier habit if you refuse to reinvest. Because the game has no confirmed Game Passes or paid multipliers, this ranking applies to every player. Each page section explains the reason, the counterexample, and the phase where the rank can flip. Treat the list as a framework for making your own decision from the live in-game prompts, not as a static shopping order.

category_mechanics_tier-list: The tier list is based on marginal value per purchase. Butter unlocks sit at S because the flavor multiplier affects every later crunch and every idle window, giving the track the widest reach. Roller upgrades sit at A because throughput is the usual bottleneck after a butter purchase, but the benefit is conditional on having enough butter and floor to process. Expansion sits at B because extra surface is only productive when a roller can cover it; the track is powerful in the mid and late game but inefficient as a first buy. Manual crunching sits at C because it is the activity that starts the loop but does not compound by itself. The ranking is phase-sensitive. In the first minutes, a roller can outrank an expensive flavor if your starter floor is already waiting. After an expansion, roller coverage can become S-tier for one or two purchases. Before logging out, the current flavor and roller combination may outrank a new expansion because offline payback matters more than active size. We deliberately do not assign tiers to unverified flavor names, roller names, or zone names. A tier label without a confirmed object would look authoritative while being fiction. Use the ranking as a lens for reading the live prompt and observing your own bottleneck.
category_advantages_tier-list: The advantage of a track-based tier list is honesty and transferability. It remains useful even when EX10 changes prices, renames a tier, or adds a new flavor because the underlying questions survive: does this purchase multiply value, fix throughput, add productive coverage, or merely keep you busy? It also helps new players understand why a cheaper upgrade can be better than a more exciting one. A tier list built from progression tracks avoids the common Roblox wiki problem of copying unverified screenshots and presenting them as permanent data. Since the game currently has no Game Passes, there is no separate whale path that would invalidate the free-player ranking. The list is also compatible with both active and idle play: butter multipliers and roller coverage affect the overnight state as well as the one-minute test. Finally, the explanation-first format gives you counterexamples. A purchase in a lower tier is not bad; it is simply more conditional. Expansion can be the correct choice after a coverage check, and manual crunching can be the best way to measure a new patch. The tier is a starting hypothesis, not a command.
category_weaknesses_tier-list: The weakness is that ranking broad tracks hides the differences between individual items. A future flavor may be cheap and efficient while another is expensive and weak, yet both would share the same broad "butter unlocks" label. We cannot resolve that until EX10 or the live game exposes verified prices and multipliers. Tier lists also encourage players to chase a letter instead of reading the current bottleneck; an S-tier flavor is not correct when the roller is already too slow to use it. The ranking can become stale after Update 2, especially if EX10 changes the economy or adds a prestige layer. We mark the list as a snapshot and expect to re-test it after the August 1 event. Finally, tier language can create the wrong emotional pressure for a relaxing ASMR simulator. Crunch My Butter has no PvP and no leaderboard requirement, so a comfortable B-tier route may be more enjoyable than an S-tier route that forces constant movement. Use the letters to organize your decision, not to turn a low-pressure game into a speedrun.

category_faq_tier-list_a_2: Expansion is powerful but conditional. New surface increases potential only when the roller can cover it and the butter value justifies the price. A player with spare roller capacity and a productive idle window may find expansion is the best choice; a player whose current floor already overwhelms the roller will usually get more value from throughput first.
category_faq_tier-list_a_3: Manual crunching is essential at the start and remains useful for measuring a route or checking a patch. It is C-tier only when treated as the entire strategy without collection or reinvestment. The activity creates the loop, but the compounding comes from buying upgrades that improve future active and offline income.
category_qt_tier-list_0: Read the tier letter together with the reason. A lower tier that fixes your bottleneck is better than an S-tier purchase you cannot use efficiently.

The game launched on June 29, 2026 under EX10 and had a recent server update on July 26, while the official Roblox Virtual Events API lists Update 2! as an active New Content event on August 1, 2026 from 17:00 to 18:30 UTC with the subtitle "Click Notify Me". That date is confirmed; the content is not. EX10 has not published patch notes, a feature list, or a code announcement for Update 2, so any article claiming specific new flavors, zones, rollers, or codes before the event is speculation. This page tracks confirmed dates, explains what to verify when the update lands, and interprets the game's unusually rapid first-month growth without turning a live snapshot into a permanent promise. The Roblox API recorded more than 5.4 million visits, 39,000 favorites, roughly 3,400 to 3,500 concurrent players, and a 93 percent approval rate by July 26. Those figures explain why players are watching the event closely, but they do not prove what EX10 will ship next. Use the Updates category as a change log and verification guide, then return to the progression categories for the mechanics that remain stable between patches.

category_mechanics_updates: The update cycle matters because Crunch My Butter is only a few weeks old and its public data is changing quickly. The official launch date establishes the baseline for the first month; the July 26 server update confirms that EX10 is actively maintaining the experience; and the August 1 Update 2 event gives players a concrete verification window. We track an update in three layers. First is the event metadata: date, time, category, and subtitle, all read from Roblox's official Virtual Events API. Second is the live game diff: new butter names, roller prompts, floor geometry, code fields, and economy behavior observed after the event. Third is the player response: visits, favorites, approval rating, and concurrent players compared with the previous snapshot. This separation prevents a common error where a community rumor becomes a "confirmed patch note" simply because it appeared in a video thumbnail. Update 2 may add content, rebalance the four-track loop, introduce a redeem field, or only fix technical issues; the event listing does not say. We publish only what survives all three layers and label unknowns clearly so readers can tell the difference between a schedule and a result.
category_advantages_updates: The advantage of following updates here is freshness with source discipline. You get an exact UTC time instead of a vague "coming soon" claim, a changelog tied to official Roblox records, and a checklist for independently verifying what changed in your own server. The growth data also gives useful context: 5.4 million visits in roughly four weeks and a 93 percent approval rate are strong signals that an update can have a large player impact, while the 8-player server cap means peak-hour queue pressure may follow a popular release. The absence of official Discord, Twitter, and YouTube links means players should not rely on a fake social account for patch notes. We link to the verified Roblox game page and EX10 group only. Finally, the update tracker makes the rest of the wiki more useful: when a patch changes a butter multiplier or roller behavior, the dated note tells you which cash-farming and tier-list advice needs re-testing. That is better than quietly leaving old numbers in place and hoping no one notices.
category_weaknesses_updates: The main weakness is that we cannot know the content of Update 2 before EX10 publishes it. A scheduled New Content event is not a patch note, and the subtitle "Click Notify Me" does not guarantee a specific reward or system. The second weakness is timing: a live game can change during the event window, and a page verified at 17:05 UTC may differ from one verified at 18:25. We record timestamps and use approximate forms for rapidly changing stats, but no static wiki can promise a permanent snapshot. The third weakness is that Roblox API counters are not a complete measure of player experience. Visits and favorites can rise while a particular mechanic becomes less satisfying, and approval percentages aggregate many kinds of feedback. We therefore treat numbers as context, not as a substitute for observation. Finally, the game is growing faster than community documentation. Videos and code pages can appear before they are verified, which creates pressure to publish quickly. Our policy is to publish a useful "unknown" rather than a fast falsehood, even if that means the update article looks less exciting on launch day.
